title: Theo Missed by $12. It Cost Him $197 📺
description:
Same $1,200 TV, same "no interest for 12 months" store card. Nora paid $100 a month and finished on time. Theo paid $99 to keep an extra dollar a month, so in month 12 he still owed $12. Because it was a deferred-interest deal, the store back-charged interest on all 12 months: about $197. His "0%" TV ended up costing $1,397.

"No interest IF paid in full" and "0% APR" are not the same thing, so check the wording before Black Friday, and divide the price by the months yourself.

Would you trust a "0%" deal after this? 👇

Follow for more numbers that change how you spend.

⚠️ Assumptions: deferred-interest store card at 30% APR (Bankrate Retail Cards Study 2025 average: 30.14%), interest worked out on each month's balance with no compounding, so real charges can be higher. How deferred interest works: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB). True 0% APR offers don't back-charge interest. Nora and Theo are fictional. Numbers are an illustration only. This is not financial advice.
